text:
alex: FYI rolled batching-selector:v2 at 14:03 UTC — immediately saw a 95p latency jump for medium prompts and a throughput drop (~22%). Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/rt/serve (alert sent by perf-bot)

susan: hitting this now in canary? or just prod? which cohort?

alex: prod only so far. medium-length chat requests (token ~256) are worst. Before: 95p ~120ms, after: 95p ~340ms. p50 stable. throughput 950 -> ~740 rps. deploy id deploy-2026-03-18-1403

kai: can you paste a trace from the slow requests? flame or timeline would help.

alex: pasted a small trace snippet from sampling (id trace-773):
```
[14:07:12] request id=abc123
kernel_select: chosen=int8_alt_kernel (latency 220ms)
kv_cache: hits=4 misses=18 evict=9
batch_wait: 180ms
infer_exec: 95ms
```

ben: that kernel name looks wrong for those shapes. int8_alt_kernel is tuned for long sequences and fused attn shapes. For medium prompt + microbatch we should be using fast-smallshape_kernel.

jordan-oncall: perf-bot alerted on 95p and tail SLO. perf-bot: "regression_detected: batching-selector:v2 -> 95p +220ms"

perf-bot: regression: metric=latency_95p, baseline=120ms, current=340ms, pct_change=+183%, notify=[eng-runtime,oncall]

kai: grabbed a perf record during the spike. Top callstacks show repeated kernel swap overhead and a bunch of kv_cache evictions triggered by microbatch reshuffle. nv-profiling shows cuda memcopy spikes between microbatches.

ben: quick grep from runtime logs shows matching pattern:
```
2026-03-18T14:05:33Z WARN kernel_selector: policy=latency_bias -> switching kernel for shape=(1,256) to int8_alt_kernel
2026-03-18T14:05:33Z INFO batcher: split microbatch -> old_batch_size=8 new_batch_size=3
2026-03-18T14:05:34Z INFO kv_cache: evict count=12456 last_evicted_key=conv-987
```

alex: interesting — batcher is splitting batches more aggressively which causes many small GPU launches + kv evictions. That lines up with memcopy spikes. Did selector start biasing toward cheaper per-token kernel at cost of microbatch amortization?

kai: yes, the new selector adds a "latency_bias" score that prefers kernels with best single-token latency for predicted points, but it forgot to account for batch formation cost and KV residency. So for medium loads it chooses a kernel that is worse amortized.

susan: can we repro locally? maybe with synthetic workload simulating 256-token requests, 10% contiguity, 60% cache hit?

ben: repro cmd i used:
```
./perf-sim --shape 1x256 --rps 800 --cache-hit 0.6 --concurrency 48 --seed 42
```
results: 95p matches production spike when selector enabled. If we pin selector to legacy scoring, 95p returns to baseline.

jordan-oncall: recommendation from oncall: rollback batching-selector:v2 in prod for now and open a follow-up to fix scoring. We already queued a canary rollback at 14:30.

alex: doing rollback now. will follow up with a postmortem and perf artifacts. tagging @kai and @ben to lead the fix for kernel scoring + KV-aware cost model.

kai: initial quick fix ideas:
- incorporate estimated batch-formation cost (launch overhead + memcopy) into kernel score
- add penalty when kv_cache eviction rate predicted > threshold
- prefer kernels that keep steady batch shapes for medium-length workloads

ben: longer term: add a micro-simulator to the selector that simulates 1s of requests and predicts amortized token cost. canary this before rollout.

perf-bot: action logged: rollback_started by alex at 14:28 UTC, incident tracking id INC-2026-0318-07.

susan: thanks. once rollback completes, can we run an AB with a telemetry build that logs kernel_switch reasons more verbosely? want to capture shape distribution and batch formation times.

alex: agree. I'll also attach traces and nvprof outputs to the incident ticket.

ben: leaving a short checklist in the ticket: reproduce locally, add kv-penalty to score, add micro-sim, unit test with mixed-shape traces, canary smaller region, full rollout.

jordan-oncall: incident resolved: rollback completed 14:35 UTC, 95p back to ~125ms. follow-up owners: kai (kernel score), ben (simulator), alex (postmortem).

alex: closing thread but leaving incident open for postmortem writeup. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
